description:
## Why

stoa-transit explicitly rejects backend.type = 'git_sha256' with "git object store is a reader-only backend". This was a design decision but the operator should be free to choose their own storage. If they want to use a git bare repo for transit block storage, that is their call.

## What

Port the git_sha256 backend from crates/reader/src/post/git_store.rs to crates/transit/src/peering/. Remove the config validation rejection in crates/transit/src/config.rs and the pipeline rejection in crates/transit/src/peering/pipeline.rs.

## Acceptance

- transit accepts backend.type = 'git_sha256' in config
- blocks written during peering are stored as git blob objects
- round-trip put/get tests pass in transit context
title: Add git_sha256 backend to stoa-transit
